name: Adversarial Three-Role Reference Composition
purpose: Test whether explicit identity, outfit, and pose role declarations reduce cross-reference leakage when every source reference contains deliberately conflicting non-target attributes.
first_party_baseline_prompt: Create a realistic full-body portrait using three project-owned references that deliberately contain conflicting non-target attributes. Use Reference 1 for recognizable identity only, Reference 2 for garment construction and palette only, and Reference 3 for joint arrangement and weight distribution only. Ignore Reference 1 clothing and pose, Reference 2 identity and pose, and Reference 3 identity and wardrobe. Place the final subject in a minimalist studio with a warm-gray backdrop and soft side light. Preserve natural anatomy, a clear garment silhouette, recognizable identity, and the target pose. Do not import the environment from any reference.

allowed_experimental_mutation_points.description: Compare implicit multi-reference use with explicit identity-only, outfit-only, and pose-only role declarations while the same adversarial reference fixtures and conflict signatures remain frozen.

reference_fixture_policy: Requires three first-party or project-owned adversarial fixtures whose target role and visually diagnostic non-target conflict attributes are preregistered before fixture generation. No private corpus image may be shipped or used as a public benchmark fixture.

provenance.notes: TB-A08 is a newly authored adversarial extension of the three-role reference-control mechanism. It does not alter historical TB-A07 or EXP-014 records.
